label: Will and CHANCE_3 at an invariant source: laws, nonvacuity, core, omissions, rivals
paraphrase: Premise-free laws and finite models (structural surrogates, not metaphysical possibility). Laws: (1) an invariant set-up excludes CHANCE_1 and CHANCE_2; (2) VG excludes every invariant two-way giver, willed or chancy; (3) VG implies DNP-prime; (4) DNP-prime excludes CHANCE_3; (5) the flip: reclassifying powers turns a willed two-way giver into a CHANCE_3 giver and conversely, with the same set-up; (6) will as a rational power and one power exclude CHANCE_3 for a being with will; (7) both are two-way giving; (8) part A: with factive giving, a necessary giver with an invariant set-up whose giving is set-up necessitated gives being at w only to necessary beings (without invariance the law does not apply); (9) with excluded middle, VG is set-up necessitation of every being at w; (10) part A: withholding, P5 and the holder's invariant set-up give a holder that is a two-way giver and not set-up necessitated, whatever its power; (11) with excluded middle, DNP-prime is exactly the absence of CHANCE_3 at w and DNP_inv exactly its absence at invariant beings; (12) with excluded middle and giving as exercise, an invariant two-way giver is willed or CHANCE_3, and not both given one power; (13) one power, CHANCE_3, intellect, will following intellect and will as a rational power are jointly inconsistent; (14) with an invariant set-up, set-up necessitation is exactly giving the same beings at every accessible world where the giver exists, and a fixed giver existing at w is set-up necessitated. Models: theist nonvacuity of arguments A-D; the chance rival (same frame and set-up, non-rational power: DNP-prime and DNP_inv fail, the conclusions of B, C and D fail); the intellectual chancer (two powers); each member of the chance core needed; omission models of arguments A-D; DNP-prime strictly stronger than DNP_inv (three worlds); VG and chance-sense nonvacuity, including one giver with CHANCE_2 and CHANCE_3 at the same world.
